title: Who Laughs with Whom? Disentangling Influential Factors in Humor Preferences across User Clusters and LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2601.03103v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Humor preferences vary widely across individuals and cultures, complicating the evaluation of humor using large language models (LLMs). In this study, we model heterogeneity in humor preferences in Oogiri, a Japanese creative response game, by clustering users with voting logs and estimating cluster-specific weights over interpretable preference factors using Bradley-Terry-Luce models. We elicit preference judgments from LLMs by prompting them to select the funnier response and found that user clusters exhibit distinct preference patterns and that the LLM results can resemble those of particular clusters. Finally, we demonstrate that, by persona prompting, LLM preferences can be directed toward a specific cluster. The scripts for data collection and analysis are publicly available to support reproducibility.

translated_title: 谁和谁一起笑？解析用户群体与大语言模型中幽默偏好的影响因素
translated_abstract: 幽默偏好在个体和文化之间存在很大差异，这使利用大语言模型（LLM）评估幽默变得复杂。在本研究中，我们通过对Oogiri（一种日本创意回应游戏）的用户投票日志进行聚类，并使用Bradley-Terry-Luce模型估计各用户群体在可解释偏好因素上的特定权重，从而对幽默偏好的异质性进行建模。我们通过提示大语言模型选择更有趣的回答来引出其偏好判断，发现不同用户群体表现出截然不同的偏好模式，且大语言模型的结果可能与特定用户群体的结果相似。最后，我们证明，通过角色提示，可以将大语言模型的偏好引导至特定用户群体。数据收集与分析脚本已公开，以支持研究的可复现性。
tldr: 该研究通过聚类分析日本创意游戏Oogiri的用户投票数据并用Bradley-Terry-Luce模型建模幽默偏好异质性，发现不同用户群体偏好模式各异、大语言模型的偏好与特定群体相似，且可通过角色提示将其幽默偏好引导至特定用户群体。
en_tdlr: This study clusters users of the Japanese creative game Oogiri via voting logs and applies Bradley-Terry-Luce models to reveal distinct humor preference patterns across user clusters, showing that LLM preferences can resemble particular clusters and can be steered toward a specific cluster through persona prompting.
